problems.title: Theorem5.3 loses derivative bandwidth variance
assumptions: p0 standard Gaussian, all relevant mixed norms finite
problems.complete_check: Almost surely distinct sampled positions. With Aij=int ci cj and S=A11+A22>0, integral ||dxx phat||^2=(2pi)^4 int[-R,R]xi^4(S+2A12 cos(2pi xi Delta))dxi. Diagonal 2SR^5/5; cross O(R^4). True p has finite H2 norm; L(phat) grows R^5 almost surely while asserted bound grows R. Success probability tends to0, contradicting3/4 for any finite allowed constant.
problems.impact: Core universal approximation theorem false; downstream proposed fast-rate proof unsupported. No direct counterexample claimed for final optimized density or coupled epsilon schedule.
problems.alternative_readings: R-dependent constant or L2-only norm changes explicit theorem. Gaussian smoothness removes regularity loophole.

correction.statement: Derivative variance and time interpolation must be reanalysed with a new parameter schedule; no replacement optimal rate asserted.

problems.title: Theorem8.11 claims mixed regularity beyond available parabolic orders
assumptions: p0 Fourier transform (1+k^2)^-2, so H3 but not stronger required mixed trace regularity
problems.complete_check: Heat solution Fourier exp(-tk^2/2)/(1+k^2)^2. Squared mixed derivative norm tail is k^(4r+2s-10): (2,4) gives6; (2,2) and(1,4) give2, all divergent. Parabolic orders (0,4),(1,2),(2,0) each give-2 and converge. Thus explicit H2_t H4_x and needed mixed constants fail under A.
problems.impact: Finite constants used in density approximation do not follow from stated initial-data assumption; core regularity premise false.
problems.alternative_readings: Theorem8.11 explicitly uses Bochner H^{m+1}(time;H^{2(m+1)}space). Reading it as weaker intersection would not supply mixed norms in Equation5.2.

correction.statement: For constant heat flow, p0 in H7 suffices for H2_t H4_x by Fourier integration. No general variable-coefficient or full learning-rate repair claimed.

problems.title: Theorem5.8 sets empirical initial discrepancy to zero
problems.complete_check: rho=p_learned-phat has rho(0)=p0-g1. In Gaussian example finite-bandwidth g1 is band-limited but p0 is not; nonzero for every finite sample realization. Zero-data energy estimate applied to rho is invalid. Residual sign checked correct.
problems.impact: Invalid step in central density-transfer proof; not a counterexample to theorem conclusion.

correction.statement: Use q=p_learned-p with zero initial value; forcing Lhat*(p-phat)+(Lhat*phat-dt phat)+(dt phat-dt p). If L(phat)<=eta^2, fitted residual<=B eta and Lhat*:H2->L2 norm<=B, forcing<= (2B+1)eta; energy gives density error<=CB eta. Does not repair P1/P2.
